That's the app, faithfully rebuilt, try PLAY, DOWNLOAD and STOP. The real thing runs on your phone.

One job, done fast

No home feed, no recommendations rabbit hole, no sign-in wall. SimpleTube opens on a search box and a big red PLAY button.

1

Paste it or say it

Paste a YouTube link, type a video name, or tap the mic and say it. Hey Google can open voice search too.

2

It just plays

PLAY starts the first result right away, at the best quality the video has, it asks for up to 2160p and takes the highest on offer. SEARCH shows the top 15 if you'd rather pick.

3

Download to keep it

Tap DOWNLOAD while it plays. The file lands on your phone and plays from its own file player, no signal needed.

Everything's in the toolbar

Options, Settings, Logs, Home, Downloads, Favorites, History, Queue, one tap each, right under the video. Nothing buried in menus.

Downloads that stay downloaded

Pick BEST, 1080p, 720p, 480p or 360p. Downloads run in the background while the stream keeps playing, queue up behind each other, resume on their own when the connection drops, and can run 1×, 2× or 4× parallel connections. A finished download is yours, it stays on the phone whether or not you tap SAVE, and the Downloads tab is a real file directory of what's actually there.

A queue that runs itself

Tap the Q on any search result, download or favorite to line it up. When a video ends, the next one starts, stream or downloaded file. Reorder with the arrows, skip when you're done with a track, and the queue survives closing the app. Queue something while nothing's playing and it starts on its own.

Voice search that plays instantly

Tap the mic, say the name, and the first result plays, no list to scroll, no keyboard popping up. There's a mic widget for the home screen too: talk, and the music starts without the app ever opening.

Keeps playing when you leave

Lock the screen or switch apps, the audio hands off to a background player and keeps going, and coming back picks the picture up at the exact spot. Minimize into a floating picture-in-picture window, and every video resumes where you left off next time you open it.

Favorites & history, with receipts

Heart anything to favorite it, from the top bar, the pause menu, or any list row. History remembers the last 50 plays and how many times you've watched each one. Pause a video and you get its description, channel and upload date, plus related videos with their own Q and Play buttons.

Locked to the video

The player can't wander off to the YouTube site, taps that would escape the video are blocked and logged, so no site ads and no accidental trips into the app-store maze. Search results sort by recent, popular, most viewed or relevance, and everything runs inside the app: no API key, no Termux, no companion apps.

A log that tells the truth

Every search, download and hiccup is written to a live terminal log, right in the app, green monospace, drag the green bar to resize it. One tap copies full diagnostics, so when something stalls you can see exactly where, instead of staring at a spinner.

Straight off the phone

Real screenshots from the Razr, the paused player with its REPLAY / PLAY / STOP overlay, and the download history with a Q, remove and favorite button on every row.

Made for the Razr's little screen

SimpleTube was built on and for the Motorola Razr 2026. Fold it shut and the app goes cover mode, the video fills the mini back screen, and the all-in-one widget puts SEARCH, QUEUE, DOWNLOADS, HISTORY, LOGS, SETTINGS and OPTIONS on that same screen, each one loading its list right inside the widget.

On the big screen it stretches out: side menus in landscape, a queue strip under the player with a red drag divider to trade space between video and playlist.

Version 1.67, the download audio fix, plus a coffee button: the muxer now writes with direct buffers and the file player sets its audio explicitly at full volume, the log reports a file's audio samples on every play, and a silent file gets flagged for re-download instead of playing quiet. Also in this build: all eight top buttons locked to one height, the description stays visible with the logs open, a single download bar at the top, a fresh launch lands on the home page, and a Buy me a cup of coffee button in Settings.
